M/S Husnabad Pisciculture, Poultry, Duckery and Housing Estate

M/S Suidsakera Fishery Co. Ltd. & Others
full_judgment:
Md. Altaf Hossain, J:- This appeal is directed against an order dated 20.5.81 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court Chittagong in Money suit No. 134 of 1980 rejecting plaintiff's prayer for attachment before judgment and releasing the Bank Guarantee furnished by the defendants. 

 2. Respondent No. 7 M/s. Husnabad Sea Fishing Industries Ltd., as plaintiff filed a suit for recovery of money from Respondents No. 1 to 6. The respondent No. 7 plaintiff's Case, in brief, was that pursuant to an agreement dated 25th March, 1978 between Bangladesh and Thailand, the appellant and defendant No. 1 (Respondent No. 1 here), nominee’s of the Governments of the two countries, formed a joint venture company under the name and Style of 'Husnabad Sea Fishing Industries Ltd. (Respondent No.7). Under the terms of the agreement setting up the joint venture Company, respondent No. 1 was to supply requisite number of trawlers to the respondent No. 7 and accordingly three Charter-parties were executed on behalf of respondent No. 1 to supply three trawlers to the respondent No. 7. In terms of the Char-ternary, the owners of the trawler would get 80% of the sale proceeds of the catch and 20% would go to the respondent No. 7 Company in which appellant's share was 51% The respondent No.1 Company owned by respondents Nos. 2-5 by practicing fraud upon the respondent No. 7 has deprived respondent No. 7 of huge amount towards their share of the catch and hence the respondent No.7 filed the suit. In that suit, the respondent No. 7 plaintiff prayed for attachment before judgment whereupon Defendents—Respondents No. 1-6 were asked to furnish security in certain sum or to show cause why they should not be required to furnish such security to produce and place at the disposal of the court when required a trawler described in the schedule of the petition. An ad-interim order of attachment was also passed in favour of the plaintiff till the security was furnished. The defendant Respondent No. 1 appeared and showed cause and also furnished a Bank Guarantee to get rid of the order of the ad-interim attachment. Before the attachment before judgment, matter was heard, at the instance of the respondent No. 7 and the appellant, the appellant, who was pro-defendant, was transposed as plaintiff and respondent No. 7 was transposed as defendant. Thereafter, the matter was heard by the learned Subordinate Judge and by the impugned order the learned subordinate Judge rejected the transposed plaintiff's prayer for attachment before judgment and also released the defendant respondent from the bank guarantee. Being aggrieved, transposed plaintiff has filed this appeal. 

 Thirdly, that the plaintiff in his petition praying for attachment before judgment has nowhere stated that defendant No. 1 trying to remove the trawler from the jurisdiction of the court with the intention to obstruct or delay the execution of the decree that might be made against it. 

 6. Mr. Asraful Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondents on the other hand submits that the learned court below has rightly rejected plaintiff-appellants prayer for attachment and has given cogent reasons for the order that he has passed. Mr. Hossain is of opinion that the learned court below has taken a correct view of law in rejecting plaintiff-appellants prayer for attachment before judgment and an interference by this court is not called for. 

 7. In respect of the first ground the learned Subordinate Judge has relied on the decision of Ramlal Sheolal v. Seth Jamaadas and other (1) The learned Advocate for the appellants submits that the present case was distinguishable from the reported decision and the principle of law enunciated in the decision should not be applied to the present case. In the Reported Decision, the appellant had brought the suit against a firm through the court of wards. On the objection of the defendant that a firm could not be used through the court of wards, the court held that the proprietor of the firm should have blend sued personally through the Manager of the court of Wards as his guardian and that defect could be remedied by an amendment. The plaintiff, thereafter, applied for amendment of the plaint, which was allowed. Previous to the order allowing amendment, the court had granted an application of the plaintiff for attachment before judgment of certain properties. It was held that when a Court holds that the suit as framed was not maintainable and the plaintiff acquiesces in that order and carries out the direction without demur and accepting the position that the suit as framed was maintainable amends the plaint, any orders passed against the defendants (e.g. attachment before judgment) before the amendment are vacated automatically. In the instant case, the defendant raised an objection that M/s. Husnabad Sea Fishing Indus-tries Ltd. had no locus-standi to file the suit and could not maintain the suit. On this objection M/s. Husnabad Pisciculture, Poultry Duckery and Housign Estate, Proforma defendant was transposed as plaintiff and the then plaintiff M/s. Husnabad Sea Fishing Industries Ltd. was transposed as defendant by an amendment. It is evident that the plaintiff acquiesced to the objection raised by the defendant. It is true that in this case there was no finding of the court that the suit was not maintainable and there was no question of acquiescing to the order of the court but the fact remains that the objection of the defendants that the suit at the instance of M/s. Husnabad Sea Fishing Industries Ltd. was not maintainable was accepted and the plaint was amended as stated above. We see no reason why the principle of law enunciated in the Nagpur case should not apply to the facts of the present case also We are of considered opinion that the order of attachment in the instant case stood automatically vacated on the day on which the pro-defendant as transposed as plaintiff and the then plaintiff (respondent No. 7) was transposed as defendant under an amendment. 

 9. As regards the third ground of ejection given by the learned Subordinate Judge, the learned Advocate for the appellant submits that the plaintiff had made out his case in paragraphs 5 and 6 of his petition for attachment before judgment. The learned Subordinate judge has observed that the plaintiff has nowhere stated that the defendant No. 1 is trying to remove the trawler from the jurisdiction of the court with intention to obstruct or delay the execution of any decree that might be passed against it and the learned Advocate could not show us from the paragraphs he relied upon that this was not correct. It is the requirement of rule 5 of Order 38 of the C.P.C. that before making an order under that rule, the court should be satisfied that the defendant with intent to obstruct or delay the execution of any decree that might be passed against him is about to remove the whole or any part of his property from the local limits of the jurisdiction of the court. The application Pit-attachment before judgment merely makes out a case that the defendant was about to remove the trawler sought to be attached from the jurisdiction of the court but fails to make out any case that he was about to remove it with intent to obstruct or delay the execution of the decree that might be passed against him. In the absence of any allegation that the defendant was removing the trawler with intent to obstruct or delay the execution of the decree that may be passed against him, the plaintiff was not entitled to an order under Order 38, Rule 5 Mr. Asrarul Hossain, the learned Advocate for the respondents has placed before us a decision of the Appellate Division in Unimarine S.A. Panan through Local Agent Bengal Shipping Line Limited and another v. Bangladesh (1) on the subject. It was held in the reported case that attachment under the rule (Order 38 Rule 5) could be made if there was an attempt on the part of the defendant to remove the property from the jurisdiction of the court with an intent to obstruct or delay the execution of the decree. As already noticed, in the case before us there was no allegation even that the trawler sought to be attached was about to be removed from jurisdiction of the court with intent to defeat or delay the execution. The learned Subordinate Judge has rightly considered this as a ground for rejecting plaintiff's application for attachment before judgment.
